heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, editing, and synchronized video production.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected split-overlay hero: full-bleed dark studio background with a layered center-left product collage and a right-side glass command panel. Show Seedream outputs as stacked cards and Seedance as a preview card with a visible play state rather than autoplay. Keep CTAs in the warm brand brown, add subtle grid lines and orbital glow accents, and make the hero feel like a premium AI production studio with dashboard-level clarity.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a dark, visual-first hero to establish premium creative control.
Use a static logo grid immediately after the hero to satisfy logo-led trust without repeating the hero pattern.
Switch from logo trust into a tabs-with-preview product module to separate image and video capabilities.
Make the first product block split and the second product block accordion-led to avoid adjacent sections feeling identical.
Use a high-contrast testimonial strip before pricing so social proof feels like an evidence layer, not a generic filler section.
End with a centered lead form on a light surface for a sharper conversion finish after darker content blocks.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative teams and enterprises that need premium visuals, audio-visual generation, and faster production workflows.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark charcoal base with layered product collage, floating capability chips, and subtle gradient depth using the brand brown accent
sections.designNote: Hero must answer what this is, who it is for, and what to do next. Keep it content-first with a strong headline, concise supporting copy, and a single solid accent CTA labeled 'Get started'. Show both image and video generation visually on the right using premium mockups, prompt-to-output tiles, and motion stills. This is the loudest section.

Use 3-6 recognizable logos in a clean static flex-wrap grid directly after the hero. Since the source data has no real logos, the layout should be a logo-ready placeholder band or fall back to a discreet metrics strip if needed. Keep it compact and highly credible, not decorative.

This section must feel like a fast 'under 60 seconds' explainer. Use 3 steps only: prompt or upload, generate or refine, export or use in production. Pair the steps with a compact preview panel showing input, generation, and output states. Keep rhythm brisk and operational, not editorial.

Use Seedream 4.5 as the first product block in a visual-first split or tabbed preview. Focus on the specific click-driving strengths: high-resolution output, typographic rendering, and multimodal image editing/composition. Because there are 5+ features, do not use a flat card grid. Show a preview panel with before/after output, then a compact feature list or tabs for deeper capability scanning.

Insert a darker proof band after the first product block to re-anchor confidence before introducing the second product. Use one sharp testimonial pull-quote or an evidence-style metric row if logo proof is unavailable. This should feel like a studio-grade validation layer, not a generic testimonial section.

Present Seedance 1.5 Pro in a contrasting layout from the image section: a visual-led accordion or stacked spotlight treatment with a video preview panel. Emphasize synchronized audio-video generation, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and faster inference. Keep motion energy higher here than in the image section.

Use this as a tight feature spotlight, not a full SaaS feature dump. Only elevate the 1-2 most click-relevant reasons: premium image quality and production-ready video generation. Use large cards with restrained copy, strong icons, and one small preview image per card. Keep the density moderate and avoid repeating the product blocks.

Since there are 4+ testimonials, use a 3-card grid with one highlighted quote and two supporting cards, or a compact carousel-static hybrid. Keep the section credibility-first and role-aware: creative director, video producer, art director, marketing manager. Avoid all cards looking the same by varying emphasis and card height.

Make pricing feel enterprise-ready and decisive. Use the two plan cards in a comparison-style layout with one accent-highlighted plan. Keep the CTA label consistent as 'Get started' everywhere, even inside pricing. The visual treatment should be darker and more conversion-led than the preceding sections.

Finish with a clean centered lead-capture card or floating panel on a light background. This is the last conversion moment, so keep it simple, high-contrast, and friction-light. The primary button must be a full-width accent button labeled 'Get started'.

If additional media or publication logos are available, use a static horizontal logo strip; otherwise omit and replace with a minimal metrics footer band. Do not use a marquee because the prompt disallows moving logo strips unless explicitly requested.

blueprint.designPersonality: A high-end AI content production studio built for enterprise buyers: dark, cinematic, and trustworthy, but structurally organized like a dashboard for clear comparison, proof, and conversion.

Add a dedicated gallery feel within product sections. Keep trust visuals logo-led and proof-driven.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Convert warm visitors by matching the ad message, proving credibility early, explaining the workflow fast, and pushing toward a single consistent action: Get started.
blueprint.narrativeMode: Continuity-first enterprise demo narrative that moves from orientation to proof to capability to conversion.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs to stay powerful without wrapping awkwardly. 56px gives it presence while protecting layout balance.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split-intent hero with brand/logo at top, large left-aligned headline block, short supporting copy, and a concise benefit list. Uses strong hierarchy and minimal clutter rather than a visual-heavy hero. Primary conversion is not embedded in the hero; the hero functions as orientation and trust framing.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Linear stacked landing-page flow with a high-contrast hero followed by a lead-capture/form block and then product-detail sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing and simple content grouping, with limited evidence of complex alternating layouts in the provided markup.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-style content card treatment with simple boxed form/card surfaces, restrained decoration, and functional emphasis over ornamental styling. Prefer standard radius, light borders or subtle shadow, and compact internal grouping.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-first pattern with a single dominant action in the hero and additional section-level CTAs for deeper conversion. Secondary actions are either absent or de-emphasized. CTA placement favors immediate visibility and repeated opportunities across key sections.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern exposed in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not represented in the provided markup; use a standard informational footer with low visual prominence if needed.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media in the hero aside from logo/branding. Product storytelling relies more on text and structured lists than on large imagery. Suitable for modular media slots, but the reference itself is text-led.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Modular product sections with repeated structure: small label, section headline, descriptive paragraph, then a bulleted feature list. Each product area is self-contained and can support its own CTA. Pattern supports progressive disclosure by introducing one product at a time.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block immediately after the hero, presented as a distinct card/surface. Form is treated as a conversion module with strong separation from the marketing content and includes hidden fields for tracking and routing.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation system is evidenced in the reference markup. If implemented, keep motion subtle and utility-oriented rather than decorative.

designNotes: Use strong typographic hierarchy with compact copy blocks.

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with a 54px headline and concise support copy
Dominant logo strip or enterprise trust bar directly under the hero
Clear dual-product positioning for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Gallery section with embedded videos and motion previews
Dedicated product feature blocks for image generation and video generation
Visible pricing/cart section with quote or demo-oriented conversion path
Testimonials placed prominently in a readable grid, not a slider
Repeated section-level CTAs that drive demo or quote requests
Compact utility-style cards for features and plans with subtle borders/shadows
avoidPatterns: Empty visual areas beside small media assets
Strip-heavy layouts that feel repetitive or visually flat
Slider-based testimonials when a grid is more readable
Overlapping content, numbered overlays, or cramped text hierarchy
Hero layouts that bury the primary value proposition
Overly ornamental design that reduces conversion clarity
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professional and enterprise buyers who need proof, clarity, and a conversion path toward evaluation, so the strategy should be product-led with strong logo-based trust. Because the content focuses on two advanced generative models, the hero should immediately frame the value proposition while the rest of the page expands on capabilities, media output, and pricing/quote intent. A split hero fits the reference pattern and supports a dark, futuristic presentation without becoming cluttered. Since the user explicitly requested a gallery section containing videos, motion previews should be a core engagement moment rather than an afterthought. Conversion should stay strong throughout the page with visible CTA repetition and a required pricing/cart or quote section to avoid past feedback issues. Testimonials should be easy to scan in a grid to improve credibility and visibility, while the overall section rhythm should remain balanced and enterprise-clean.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
